 MISSOULA, Mont. — Montana returns home after a bye week and a road win at Eastern Washington, carrying momentum from a 42-33 result in Cheney that included a program-record 11 sacks.
 The Grizzlies used that defensive pressure to help set the tone against Eastern Washington, and they now head into Saturday’s 1:00 p.m. home game against Portland State (2-7 overall, 2-4 Big Sky) with the regular season nearing its end.
 Sophomore linebacker Colton Lentz said the extra preparation made a difference.
 "I think we executed the game plan very well, having that bye week and that extra week to prep and prepare for this game. I think it really helped us out. And I mean, obviously it felt great being out there and contributing to the team. So I mean, overall it felt great," Lentz said.
 Montana has won the last six meetings with Portland State, but the Vikings bring several threats into Missoula.
 Terence Loville ranks sixth in Big Sky for receiving, Delon Thompson ranks seventh in rushing and pass rusher Avery Ducsik ranks second in sacks behind UM's Tyler King.
 Head coach Bobby Kennedy said Portland State’s skill players and return game stood out.
 "Their offense, number three (Loville), their wide receiver is an explosive guy. They've got good players. I think the sack leader in our conference on defense. And then also the returners on special teams are guys that can create explosive plays and take to the house at any time. So this is going to be a good challenge for us," Kennedy said.
 Senior wide receiver Landon Ransom-Goelz said Montana also brings added motivation back to Wa-Griz.
 "It's always good playing in WA-Griz know. We lost the last time so you know we're going to come here obviously with little chip on our shoulder because I feel like we have more to prove, you know, like BK says every week we're not a finished product. So we're still getting better and going out there and just showing out what we're working on week to week to the fans," Ransom-Goelz said.
 Montana will host Portland State on Saturday at 1:00 p.m. as the Grizzlies try to carry their recent form into the postseason push.
